name: PT Lippo Cikarang Tbk

frontmatter.title: Lippo Cikarang: land net of advances, earnings reset to the run-rate, discount at the band midpoint
frontmatter.summary: The red team was right on the asset value: our RNAV added the land bank gross of customer advances and dated the asset side a year before the liability side. We deduct the advances, mark the land to the latest balance sheet, rebuild FY2026 from the nine months delivered and carry the working capital those nine months actually absorbed. Value falls to Rp441 against Rp424: HOLD, no longer a buy.
thesis: RNAV is land less net debt AND customer advances: IDR1,026.5bn current and IDR846.6bn non-current at June 2026 are the buyer's cash for stock still in the land bank, so valuing the land gross counts the same rupiah twice [S3 p.5].

The earnings base is the nine months delivered, not a re-priced FY2025: FY2026E revenue of IDR3,165.8bn and EBITDA of IDR307.3bn add a fourth quarter at the nine-month average revenue with opex normalised for a one-off third-quarter charge [S0].

The land is still worth more than the price: IDR2,177.1bn of market capitalisation against a net landbank of carrying value less a haircut and the advances, and the stock is at 0.3x times book [S0][S2 p.115].
Control is absolute and the float is 9.3%, so the corporate action the exchange's minimum forces is a per-share event: a discounted rights issue dilutes, a tender could close the discount [S9][S8].
The target is the band midpoint, not the top: 55.0% to RNAV, then the engine's liquidity discount of 20.0%, giving Rp441 and 3.9% [S0].

catalysts.event: Full-year 2026 marketing-sales release against the company target - the kill criterion on order intake
FY2026 audited results, the fourth-quarter margin and the dividend decision
Free-float compliance deadline for issuers below the small-capitalisation threshold; any rights issue or controller sell-down

blocks.text: This is a revision, not a new view, and it changes the rating. The red team found one fatal and thirteen material faults; we accept the fatal one in full. Our RNAV added the land bank gross of customer advances, and the advances are the buyers' money for stock that is still in that land bank, so the same rupiah was counted twice. We now deduct total contract liabilities at the last disclosed date, mark the land to the 30 September 2026 balance sheet instead of December 2025, and rebuild the earnings from the nine months actually delivered. The result is an HOLD rating at a target of Rp441 against Rp424, 3.9%, down from a buy at a target that no longer survives its own arithmetic.

What the correction does to the valuation is visible in one line. The RNAV method, after the developer discount of 55.0%, is Rp576; the weighted value is Rp481, rolled forward to Rp545 and cut by the liquidity discount of 20.0% to Rp441. The initiation's valuation section called the post-discount figure the pre-discount one, which made the build impossible to follow; the bridge is now written in the order the engine computes it.

The variant view that survives is narrower than before. Lippo Cikarang owns serviced township land inside a working industrial estate in Cikarang, carries it at cost, and trades at a discount to what that land and the fee stream are worth after every deduction we can source. That gap is real but it is not large enough to pay for the wait: the discount sits at the midpoint of the band the method card allows, the earnings are falling back to the order run-rate, and the one event that could close the gap is a corporate action whose terms are unknown. The price already reflects most of the asset value, and the bear case now lands below the price rather than at it.

What would make this a buy again is specific: a marketing-sales print above the company's target, a land transaction or appraisal that puts a sourced price on the serviced hectares, or a tender from the controlling shareholder at a price above the current one. None of those is in the base case.

PT Lippo Cikarang Tbk is an integrated township developer in Cikarang, Bekasi, on the eastern edge of the Jakarta conurbation. It listed in 1997 and runs three lines of business — real-estate development, real-estate management and services, and fund management and investment through subsidiaries [S2 p.23]. The estate combines industrial parks under the Delta Silicon name, residential clusters, commercial centres, and the utilities and estate management that hold the township together [S2 p.26].

Industrial land is developed inside the township but not all of it is owned outright. A subsidiary operates one of the Delta Silicon estates under a joint operation with the landowner, PT Cikarang Hijau Indah, which contributes the land while the company plans, builds, markets and manages it [S2 p.151]. That structure gives the company a fee and a profit share rather than the full land margin, and it is why industrial presales are reported separately from residential.

The economics are lopsided. In FY2025 the real-estate segment produced net revenue of IDR3,944.6bn and gross profit of IDR624.7bn, while support services produced IDR474.5bn of revenue and IDR58.2bn of gross profit [S2 p.152]. Support services are an estate-management annuity: they grow with the occupied area, carry a thin margin, and are not exposed to the handover timetable that swings development revenue.

Marketing sales, the company's order-intake KPI, were IDR1,649.0bn in FY2025 against IDR1,643.0bn in FY2024 and IDR1,301.0bn in FY2023 [S2 p.49][S4 p.17][S5]. Residential accounted for IDR1,040.0bn of the FY2025 figure and industrial land for IDR68.0bn [S2 p.42]; the balance is commercial and shophouse product. Orders convert to revenue only on handover, which is why a year of resilient orders can sit beside falling recognised revenue.

The balance sheet is the business. Inventories were IDR8,404.5bn at December 2025, of which land under development with a saleable area of 226 ha hectares sits entirely inside Lippo Cikarang [S2 p.136], alongside land for development carried at IDR246.3bn [S2 p.142]. The company also owns investment properties carried at cost of IDR252.4bn [S2 p.115]. That is the asset base the valuation is built on, and it is why we value the company on its parts rather than on a single earnings stream.

The company employed 280.0 people at the end of FY2025 [S2 p.36]. Control sits with PT Kemuning Satiatama at 89.0% of the shares, the ultimate beneficial owner being James T. Riady, and the company is part of the Lippo group [S2 p.37]. The public holds the remainder, and only 9.3% is held in blocks below the five per cent disclosure threshold [S2 p.37].

Strategy is to keep selling land and built product inside the township, grow the management fee stream, and hold the IDR1,700.0bn marketing-sales target for 2026 [S2 p.49]. Within Cikarang the company is the incumbent estate with the deepest infrastructure; nationally it is a challenger to the large Jakarta developers. Its advantage is location, permits and installed infrastructure; its limitation is that it owns one township and cannot redeploy capital geographically.

Demand for the township comes from three engines: household formation and mortgage-funded purchases in Greater Jakarta; manufacturing relocation into the Bekasi-Karawang corridor, which buys industrial land; and the logistics and data-centre build-out that has lifted warehouse and power-intensive land demand around Cikarang [S2 p.26]. The company presents the estate as an industrial, commercial and residential cluster with supporting infrastructure, which is the right frame for a land seller whose buyer mix moves with the manufacturing cycle [S2 p.23].

Our macro deck has Indonesian real GDP growth of 5.3 rate%, consumer inflation of 3.3 rate% and a policy rate of 5.75% with no cuts through the forecast, against a rupiah at Rp17,570/USD to the dollar in 2026. The company's own discussion ties residential demand to mortgage affordability and industrial demand to the estate's tenant base [S2 p.43]. We use the deck unchanged: no rate relief is assumed, and that is the main reason our revenue forecast falls before it stabilises.

The rate path is the single most important external variable for residential absorption. With the policy rate held at 5.75% in our deck, we do not assume a mortgage-driven recovery, and we treat the company's plan for single-digit revenue and operating-income growth in 2026 [S2 p.49] as a pre-first-half target that the actuals have already contradicted [S3 p.6]. That is a forecast judgement, not a view on management: the plan was set with the annual report and the market moved against it.

Property revenue also bears a final tax deducted before net revenue — IDR100.1bn in FY2025 [S2 p.116] — so headline prices overstate what the developer keeps, and the tax cannot be passed on in a soft market. Land acquisition, permits and the estate's industrial status are governed by national and regional rules the company does not control, and the annual report flags regulatory change as a risk to the development timetable [S2 p.43]. Capital-market rules matter too: the exchange has raised the minimum public shareholding to 15 per cent, which affects a stock with a 9.3% float [S9].

The competitive set is the other Bekasi and Karawang estates — Jababeka and the MM industrial park among them — plus the newer Batang and Subang parks and the listed township developers of Greater Jakarta. We have no sourced market-share series for Cikarang and the company does not publish one, so we do not claim a share. What the filings do show is a land bank concentrated in one estate and an order intake that has been broadly flat for three years [S2 p.49][S4 p.17].

The moat is location, infrastructure and permits. An industrial tenant that has built a factory inside the estate does not move for a small land-price difference, and the estate's utilities, roads and management are a recurring fee the residents and tenants pay [S2 p.26]. Against that, rivalry among corridor estates is high, buyers of large industrial parcels are few and negotiate hard, and the developer has no pricing power in a downturn. Landowners and contractors are fragmented, so supplier power is moderate; new entrants need scale, permits and infrastructure, a real barrier; substitutes are other corridors and other forms of industrial space, which cap land-price increases.

The external swing factors are the policy rate and mortgage availability for residential, the manufacturing and data-centre investment cycle for industrial land, and the rupiah for imported building materials. The company's debt is all rupiah-denominated [S2 p.144], so currency moves hit costs rather than the balance sheet. We assume the manufacturing cycle stays intact and the rate path stays where the deck has it; if either breaks, the bear case is the relevant one, not a revision of the base.

Revenue has been a handover story rather than a demand story. It rose from IDR1,243.6bn in FY2022 to IDR1,028.8bn in FY2023, IDR1,890.6bn in FY2024 and IDR4,419.1bn in FY2025, a 133.7% jump that came from delivering the apartment and Meikarta backlog rather than from a step-up in orders [S2 p.45]. Order intake in the same years was IDR1,301.0bn, IDR1,643.0bn and IDR1,649.0bn [S5][S4 p.17][S2 p.49] — broadly flat while recognised revenue more than tripled.

That mismatch explains the margin. FY2025 gross margin was 15.5% and EBITDA margin 6.2%, against 46.7% in FY2023, because the backlog was delivered at low margin [S0]. The first half of 2026 shows the other side: net revenue of IDR1,590.0bn against IDR2,188.3bn, gross profit of IDR476.1bn against IDR427.2bn, opex of IDR227.0bn and net profit of IDR228.4bn against IDR208.2bn [S3 p.6]. Revenue fell while gross profit and net profit rose; the residential mix, not volume, did that.

The margin inputs are now like-for-like on the segment that generates them. Development gross margin is 26.5% in FY2026E, which is the H1 2026 development segment's own margin after final tax — the real-estate segment's own net revenue and gross profit — not the blended group figure and not a haircut to it [S3 p.80]; it fades to 23.0% as the remaining low-margin apartment stock is handed over. Recurring gross margin is 41.7%, the H1 2026 support-services margin, stepping down as the estate contracts renew [S3 p.80-81]. SG&A is 20.5% of revenue, between the first-half ratio and the nine-month ratio that includes the third-quarter charge [S3 p.6][S0]. Depreciation was IDR51.7bn in FY2025 and IDR22.5bn in FY2024 on the segment note, not the smaller amounts the data pack carries, because the direct cash-flow method used in the LK does not show the full charge [S2 p.152]. Capital expenditure was IDR21.1bn and IDR5.2bn on the company's definition, which includes investment-property additions [S2 p.152]. Both lines are small against revenue but they matter for the EBITDA-to-cash bridge, and we restate them rather than model around the pack.

The working-capital engine is inventory and customer advances, and it absorbs cash, not releases it. Inventories of IDR8,404.5bn at December 2025 had fallen further by 30 September 2026 [S0]; contract liabilities were IDR1,026.5bn current and IDR846.6bn non-current at June 2026 [S3 p.5], down from a higher balance at December 2025 as advances were earned into revenue. The cash record is the evidence: operating cash flow was IDR-928.9bn in FY2025 after an inflow of IDR81.4bn in FY2024 [S2 p.45], and in the first nine months of 2026 it was roughly zero while net debt rose to the reported position [S0]. We therefore hold operating working capital as a flat rupiah stock rather than a revenue ratio: FY2026E carries a build of IDR244.2bn that takes it to IDR6,204.0bn, the same absorption the nine months actually delivered, and leaves FY2026E free cash flow at IDR7.5bn — effectively the zero the company printed — with net debt at IDR264.3bn against the reported position. From FY2027E the stock is held flat in rupiah, so the bridge carries no working-capital swing in either direction. A working-capital ratio of zero, which the prior draft used, would have released the entire IDR5,959.8bn stock into cash in one year and printed net cash on a company that is borrowing to fund inventory.

Interest cover on recurring income is thin on the audited year and adequate on the current halves. FY2025 support-services gross profit of IDR58.2bn against the year's financial charges is cover of about one and a fifth times before any of that segment's own costs [S2 p.152, p.35]. The two half-year segment notes tell a different story: support services earned an operating profit after their own cost load in both halves, which covers the annual financial charges several times over [S3 p.80-81]. The group net debt to EBITDA of 0.9 is flattered by handover EBITDA and we do not lean on it: the recurring stream is the only line that would survive a presales winter.

The balance sheet is conservative for a developer. At December 2025 cash was IDR419.1bn against debt of IDR660.3bn, net debt of IDR241.2bn and net debt to EBITDA of 0.9 [S0]. The bank loans are short-term, all rupiah, and secured on land; the working-capital facility from Bank Tabungan Negara carries a single-digit rate and matures within a year [S2 p.144]. Equity attributable to the parent was IDR6,686.6bn, or Rp1,302 per share, after the 2025 rights issue priced at Rp500 [S2 p.10][S2 p.116].

Capital allocation has been balance-sheet repair rather than distribution, and the 2025 rights issue now has a documented use. The limited public offering was priced at Rp500; the FY2025 statement of changes in equity shows it adding share capital against a charge to additional paid-in capital, a net contribution that took the share count to 5,134.7 million [S2 p.116, note 25]. The proceeds were downstreamed as capital into PT Megakreasi Cikarang Permai and on into PT Mahkota Sentosa Utama, with the working-capital portion two-thirds realised at the year end [S2 p.51]. That matters for valuation: the book behind our P/BV cross-check is cash paid in and land at cost, not a related-party mark — but the cash was injected into an entity under common control that also sells commercial land to the company.

We rebuilt the year from the nine months that exist rather than from a growth rate. The nine-month revenue total was well below the prior-year nine-month base and nine-month EBITDA was a fraction of the prior year; the third quarter alone carried a net loss and an operating-expense line roughly three times the first-half quarterly rate [S0]. FY2026E adds a fourth quarter at the nine-month average quarterly revenue, with operating expenses set at 20.5% of revenue rather than the higher ratio the nine months printed, on the assumption that the third-quarter charge is non-recurring: revenue of IDR3,165.8bn and EBITDA of IDR307.3bn [S0]. That normalisation is the one soft assumption in the build and we state it plainly: holding the nine-month opex ratio instead, on the same revenue and gross profit, gives EBITDA about one-tenth lower and takes a similar share off EPS — which is the sensitivity the bear case carries. The prior draft's basis, that the change was the nine-month run-rate annualised, was arithmetically false; annualising nine months gives a fall of roughly three-tenths on total revenue, and the development line falls further because the recurring base grew.

This is below the company's own plan, and deliberately so. Management targeted single-digit revenue and operating-income growth for 2026 [S2 p.49], but the first half has since printed revenue below the prior-year period with the profit improvement coming from mix [S3 p.6]. We follow the actual, not the plan. If the second half delivers the guidance, our numbers are conservative rather than wrong, and the bull case captures that.

The earnings-quality screen is clean on the manipulation tests and flagged on optics. On accruals, FY2025 net profit of IDR215.8bn against operating cash of IDR-928.9bn, and FY2024 net profit of IDR-1,612.5bn against IDR81.4bn, show swings that track inventory and advance timing rather than a receivable build [S2 p.45]. Two one-offs drive the reported history: the IDR1,701.2bn DINFRA settlement loss in FY2024 that turned the year negative, and an inventory impairment of IDR17.1bn [S2 p.150]. Related-party operating expenses are limited to entities under common control and were a small share of total opex at the half year [S3 p.52]. Investment properties are at cost and property is not revalued, so book value is not inflated by a revaluation [S2 p.115]. We found no special notation letter or special-monitoring status in the filings [S2][S3]. Verdict: optics-class flags only, no manipulation-class flag.

A land-backed developer is valued on its assets, not its earnings. Development revenue is recognised on handover and swings with mix, so a trailing multiple on a year that delivered a low-margin backlog is close to meaningless. We weight RNAV at 60%, with the earnings and book multiples at 20% and 20% as market cross-checks taken from the stock's own history rather than from peers, because the float is too thin for peer-relative pricing to carry weight [S0].

The cost of capital is built from the house macro deck and the company's own debt terms. The risk-free rate is 7.4%, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2% and the country risk premium 2.5%, giving a cost of equity of 13.5% on a levered beta of 1.15 from an unlevered 0.90. Debt costs 9.4% before tax at the marginal rate of 22.0%, and gearing of 26.0% debt to 74.0% equity gives a WACC of 11.9% [S2 p.144]. That is the nominal rupiah rate at which the model rolls the target forward; it is high, which is appropriate for a small-cap developer with a concentrated asset base.

The asset value starts from the balance sheet, and now from the same balance-sheet date on both sides. We take inventories at 30 September 2026 [S0] plus land for development of IDR246.3bn [S2 p.142], apply a haircut for selling costs, the final property tax and the net-realisable-value risk that the FY2024 impairment evidences [S2 p.150], and then deduct total customer advances of IDR1,026.5bn current plus IDR846.6bn non-current at June 2026 [S3 p.5]. The advances, IDR1,026.5bn and IDR846.6bn, are the buyer's money for stock that is still in the land bank; leaving them out counts the same rupiah twice, which is why the peer files in this sector set their land value net of advances. We add nothing for appraisal uplift because the LK already carries the stock at the lower of cost and realisable value [S2 p.115].

The recurring stream is capitalised on its operating profit, not its gross profit. H1 2026 support services produced gross profit, its own segment operating expenses and an operating profit after them of roughly three-quarters of gross profit [S3 p.80]. We keep the engine's gross-profit formula and set the cap rate at 15.7%, which is a twelve per cent cap on that operating profit — about eight times pre-tax segment earnings for a contracted township-management and utility stream. The prior draft capitalised gross profit at nine per cent and therefore valued the segment at nearly fifteen times its net operating profit, which is the fault the red team identified. Net debt is deducted at the reported level [S0] and the result divided by 5,134.7 million shares.

The bridge, in the order the engine computes it: gross RNAV is the gross figure per share; the developer discount of 55.0% takes the RNAV method to Rp576; weighting the three methods gives a fundamental value of Rp481; that is rolled forward one year at the cost of equity to Rp545; and the liquidity discount of 20.0% for average daily turnover of IDR232.1m takes it to Rp441 against Rp424 — 3.9% and an HOLD rating [S0]. The initiation wrote the post-discount figure as the pre-discount one and misdescribed the stacked discount; both are corrected here.

The discount is set against the name's own record, not asserted. At Rp424 the stock is at a discount of about two-thirds to RNAV per share, and the RNAV-discount band the method card allows for IDX developers runs from two-fifths to seven-tenths, so the current level sits at the wide end. The stock also trades at 0.3x times book against the low end of its own five-year P/BV range [S0]. We therefore target the midpoint of the band — 55.0% — and reach the wide end only through the engine's liquidity rule. A band-midpoint target is not a call that the discount closes; it is the level the stock has historically returned to.

The two cross-checks diverge, and we explain rather than average them away. The P/E method returns Rp214, -62.9% against the primary, because it applies the stock's own mean multiple of 11.9 times to trailing earnings that carry the second-half 2025 loss and a weak 2026 quarter. On our FY2026E EPS of 38.9 the stock trades at 10.9x, and that same multiple on forward earnings would sit above the RNAV. The P/E method therefore brackets the answer from below; it does not anchor it. The P/BV method returns Rp462, -19.8%, at 0.3 times book, which is where the stock has traded through most of the past two years [S0]. It is the closest of the three to the market and the least informative, because the book is land at cost.

The sensitivity confirms that the target is driven by the discount and the land value rather than by the near-term margin. A shift in the RNAV discount moves the target by more than a similar shift in the development margin, which is why we spent the analytical effort on the landbank and the discount rather than on quarterly handover timing.

At Rp424 the market capitalisation is IDR2,177.1bn, far below the IDR8,404.5bn of inventory the group carried at cost on 31 December 2025 and the lower stock reported at 30 September 2026 [S0][S2 p.115]. Read as a reverse valuation, the price implies that the market expects either a permanent impairment of the land stock or a discount wider than the top of the method card's band. We do not think the evidence supports that: the first half showed the estate selling product at a better margin, and the balance sheet carried net debt of IDR241.2bn at 31 December 2025 rising to IDR264.3bn at 30 September 2026 [S0], while the dividend is zero, so there is no distribution yield to justify a separate premium.

Two method limits are worth stating. The RNAV depends on the carrying value being realisable, which is a judgement the FY2024 impairment shows is not automatic; and the liquidity discount is a rule, not a valuation — with a float of 9.3% it can widen as easily as it narrows [S0][S9].

The largest company-specific risk is not property, it is the share register. The controlling shareholder holds 89.0% and the free float is 9.3% [S2 p.37], below the minimum of 15 per cent the exchange now requires [S9]. For an issuer below the small-capitalisation threshold the deadline is 31 March 2029, and OJK has said it will consider extensions where market absorption is weak [S9][S8]. The consequence is a forced corporate action, and we now put it in the bear case rather than in a footnote: a rights issue struck at a discount dilutes per-share asset value, and we test a share increase; a controller sell-down adds supply to a stock with average daily turnover of IDR232.1m [S0]. The mirror of that in the bull case is a tender: the controller itself subscribed at Rp500 in the 2025 rights issue, above today's Rp424, which is the controller's own mark on the asset and the reason we test a share reduction as well as an increase [S2 p.10].

Macro is the second risk. Our deck holds the policy rate at 5.75% with no cuts and Indonesian growth at 5.3 rate%; if rupiah pressure forces the central bank to tighten instead, mortgage-funded residential demand falls first [S2 p.43]. The rupiah at Rp17,570/USD raises imported material costs but not the debt, which is all rupiah [S2 p.144]. A weaker currency is therefore a margin risk, not a solvency risk.

Operationally the company owns one township. Absorption depends on industrial tenants continuing to take land and households continuing to buy clusters; a slowdown in either shows up as inventory and impairment, which the FY2024 charge of IDR17.1bn demonstrates [S2 p.150]. The Meikarta legacy is a second operational tail: the contract-liability balance is being recognised and the margin on those deliveries was poor [S2 p.45]. We could not source a first-half 2026 marketing-sales figure from any reachable outlet, so we cannot yet test order intake against the IDR1,700.0bn target; that is a gap in the evidence, not a negative finding.

Governance risk is the related-party balance sheet, and it is larger than the disclosures suggest. The FY2024 IDR1,701.2bn loss is a common-control business combination, not a settlement with a third party: MKCP took a controlling stake in MSU by extinguishing the Bowsprit DINFRA investment at a disclosed exchange value and booked the difference [S2 note 10.b, note 36]. The counterparty is an entity under common control, the assets received are carried at the exchange value, and no independent valuation is disclosed; the group also buys commercial land from the same entity [S2 p.51]. The 2025 rights-issue proceeds were injected into that chain [S2 p.51]. Operating flows to affiliates are modest at the half year — services from PT Multipolar, cash at Bank Nationalnobu, financing from Asiatic Sejahtera Finance [S3 p.52] — so the channel that matters is the balance sheet, not the P&L. We classify it as a structure flag, disclosed but not independently valued, and it is why we do not mark the land to an appraisal and why the bear case carries a land write-down. We found no share pledge disclosed and no special notation or monitoring-board status in the filings we archived [S2][S3].

Regulatory and tax risks are the final tax on property revenue of IDR100.1bn in FY2025, deducted before net revenue [S2 p.116], and the land and permit process for new phases, which the company flags as a timetable risk [S2 p.43]. Liquidity risk is that a 9.3% float supports a market capitalisation of IDR2,177.1bn but turnover of IDR232.1m, so a position of any size moves the price.

The scenarios are mirrored and now carry the drivers that matter. The bear case lowers presales growth, widens the discount, marks the landbank down and adds the discounted rights issue; the bull case moves the same four drivers the other way, with industrial and data-centre demand marking the land up and a tender removing shares. Probabilities are a half in the base case and a quarter on each tail. The bear case is not a crisis scenario — it is the same company with slower absorption, a wider discount, a write-down and dilution — and it now lands below the current price, which is what a bear case should do. The bull case does not assume a re-rating beyond the top of the method card's band.

What would change the view: marketing sales landing at or above the company's target, which would pull recognised revenue up from FY2027E and lift the landbank out of its discount; a gross margin holding above the first-half level once the low-margin tail is gone; an announced tender or sell-down at a price above the current one, which would resolve the float overhang and could remove a discount rather than add one; and a sourced land transaction inside the township that puts a price per square metre on the serviced hectares.

Control is absolute. PT Kemuning Satiatama holds 89.0% of the 5,134.7 million shares and the ultimate beneficial owner is James T. Riady [S2 p.37]. The public holds the rest, of which only 9.3% sits in blocks below the five per cent disclosure line [S2 p.37]. No commissioner or director owned shares in 2025 [S2 p.36].

The free float is below the exchange's raised minimum [S9]. For an issuer of this market capitalisation the transition allows until the 2029 deadline to reach the new threshold, with OJK retaining discretion to extend where the market cannot absorb the supply [S9][S8]. The practical routes are a rights issue — the company has already used one, at Rp500 in 2025 [S2 p.10] — or a controller sell-down. Either changes the per-share arithmetic, which is why we carry it as a valuation risk rather than a governance footnote.

Related-party dealings are disclosed and modest. Operating expenses to entities under common control were a small share of total opex at the half year, the largest line being services from PT Multipolar, and the group also places cash with Bank Nationalnobu and finances through Asiatic Sejahtera Finance [S3 p.52]. Associates include PT Hyundai Inti Development, held through the group's property investments [S3 p.53]. Sales to related parties are not a material share of revenue on the disclosures we read.

The auditor is KAP Amir Abadi Jusuf, Aryanto, Mawar & Rekan, part of the RSM network, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2024 statements and was reappointed for FY2025; the audit fee was 897 IDR m million [S2 p.39][S2 p.59]. Investment properties are at cost, so there is no revaluation cushion in book value [S2 p.115]. We found no special notation letter or special-monitoring-board status in the annual report or the half-year statements [S2][S3].

The dividend record is a blank: nothing paid in the years we model and a trailing dividend of 0.0 [S0], within a policy that pays only a capped share of profit [S2 p.49]. On ESG, the material exposures are water and flood management across a low-lying estate, construction safety, and the land-acquisition record. The annual report describes the estate infrastructure and community programmes, but we found no sustainability report or emissions disclosure in the archive [S2 p.43]. We report that as thin evidence rather than as a clean bill.

The dated events that matter are the FY2026 audited results and the dividend decision at the annual meeting, expected in the first quarter of 2027 [S2 p.49]; the full-year marketing-sales release, which the company has historically published early in the following year [S5][S6]; and the free-float milestones, with a final deadline of 31 March 2029 for an issuer of this size [S9]. Any announcement of a rights issue or a controller sell-down would be the single most important disclosure for the share price [S2 p.10].

Our kill criterion is on marketing sales, dated and actionable: if the FY2026 marketing-sales print is below the IDR1,700.0bn company target [S2 p.49], the order-intake case fails and we move to reduce the name regardless of the asset value, because the landbank discount only closes if the estate keeps selling. A print at or above the target with a residential share of at least the FY2025 level would let us raise the presales path for FY2027E instead. The test is applied at the full-year release and again at the FY2026 results, and we do not revise it between prints on the strength of a single quarter. We could not source a first-half 2026 marketing-sales figure from any reachable outlet, so the order intake for the current year is untested — that is a gap in the evidence, not a negative finding.

Between updates we watch four numbers with thresholds. Marketing sales against the IDR1,700.0bn target, as above. The contract-liability balance, which is the forward revenue line — IDR1,026.5bn current and IDR846.6bn non-current at June 2026 [S3 p.5]; a second consecutive half of decline below that level would confirm the handover tail is running out faster than we model. The development gross margin, held at 26.5% for 2026 and fading to 23.0% [S3 p.80]; two halves below that path would mean the residential mix is not holding. And inventories, already lower at 30 September 2026 than at the prior year end [S0], where a further impairment charge would signal that absorption is failing. We will also re-check the share register at each annual report, because the float is the swing factor in the target.

bear.narrative: Presales stall as the policy rate stays on the house path and mortgage affordability bites; the float deadline forces a discounted rights issue that adds about a tenth to the share count or a controller sell-down into a 9.33% free float, the land bank takes the write-down a stalled township would justify against a Cikarang industrial-land price that stops rising, and the discount stays at its widest for another cycle.

bull.narrative: Data-centre and industrial demand around Cikarang lifts industrial-land prices and presales; the township's industrial land sells faster, the land bank marks up against the same price series, and the controller uses the 89% control to take the float out through a tender, cutting the share count and narrowing the discount by ten points.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: The engine's presales line is the revenue-equivalent handover value, not the marketing-sales KPI. FY2025 real-estate net revenue was Rp3,944.6bn against marketing sales of Rp1,649bn [S2 p.49, p.152] because the apartment and township backlog was handed over. FY2026E of -33.3% is set from the actual: nine-month 2026 net revenue of Rp2,375.3bn [S0, quarterly lines] plus a fourth quarter at the nine-month average quarterly revenue gives about Rp3,167bn for the year, and stripping the recurring stream leaves the development line. Marketing sales have been flat at Rp1,301bn, Rp1,643bn and Rp1,649bn across FY2023-FY2025 [S5, S4, S2 p.49] against a Rp1,700bn 2026 target [S2 p.49], and contract liabilities fell from Rp2,611bn at December 2025 to Rp1,873bn at June 2026 [S3 p.5], so handovers converge on the new-sales rate: -10% in FY2027E, then flat to +2% as the estate's industrial land and township services carry the base.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because the driver series above is already the handover value recognised in the year, not orders taken. The recognition lag (presales are recognised one to two years later on handover) is captured in the driver itself, which is why FY2025 revenue of Rp3,944.6bn sits far above the Rp1,649bn of marketing sales signed that year [S2 p.49, p.152].

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Support-services revenue was Rp335.1bn in H1 2026 against Rp300.8bn in H1 2025, +11.4% [S3 p.80-81], so FY2026E is set at +12.7% to the H1 run-rate rather than the +41% that annualising H1 alone would give. From FY2027E we hold 5% and then 4%, in line with the estate's occupied area, because the FY2025 jump to Rp474.5bn included the new Cosmopolis area management contract [S2 p.17, p.152] and will not repeat annually.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Like-for-like on the development segment, not the blended group figure: H1 2026 real-estate net revenue was Rp1,268.8bn after Rp32.9bn of final tax and real-estate gross profit was Rp336.4bn, a 26.5% margin on the same scope [S3 p.80]. We open FY2026E at that 26.5%, not at a haircut to it, and fade to 25.0%, 24.0%, 23.0% through FY2030E as the low-margin apartment stock in the land bank is handed over ahead of the residential launches. FY2025's own development segment margin of 15.8% (gross profit Rp624,736m on revenue Rp3,944,604m) [S2 p.152] was the apartment-and-Meikarta mix and is not the current economics.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: H1 2026 support-services gross profit of Rp139.7bn on net revenue of Rp335.1bn is 41.7% [S3 p.80], against 55.2% in H1 2025 [S3 p.81], so the stream earns a wide margin but is fading. FY2026E holds the H1 2026 actual and then steps down to 39%, 37%, 36% and 35% as the estate-services contracts are renewed, which is below both observed half-years and is the one cost-load we apply. FY2025's full-year 12.3% [S2 p.152] is not comparable: it implies a gross loss in the second half that its own first half does not show, so we anchor on the two half-year segment notes that reconcile to the consolidated totals.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: 15.7% on recurring gross profit, which is a 12% cap rate on the segment's operating profit after its own cost load, given the H1 2026 ratio of segment operating profit to gross profit of 0.75x [S3 p.80]; see params cap_rate_basis. The LK carries investment properties at cost, Rp252.4bn, with no fair-value disclosure [S2 p.115], so the capitalised income net of the segment's own costs is the defensible value for that stream.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: 55%, the midpoint of the 40-70% band the property-developer method card sets for IDX developers. Against the name's own five-year record the current Rp424 price is a 67% discount to the corrected RNAV per share, i.e. at the wide end of the band, and 0.32x book against a five-year P/BV range of 0.23-0.44x [S0 history_multiples] - so the band's midpoint, not its top, is the target. The engine applies its own 20% liquidity discount on top for Rp0.2bn average daily turnover, which takes the effective discount to about 64%, near the wide end: the wide end is reached through the liquidity rule, not by stacking a second haircut here.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 operating expenses of Rp545.1bn on net revenue of Rp2,375.3bn is 22.9% [S0], inflated by a third-quarter charge that was roughly three times the first-half quarterly rate. H1 2026 alone was 14.3% of revenue [S3 p.6]. FY2026E is set at 20.5%, between the two, so overhead is not flattered by the first half nor burdened by a quarter we cannot source as recurring, and held flat because it is a largely fixed township overhead carried against a shrinking revenue base.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation of Rp51.7bn [S2 p.152 note 39] on gross revenue of Rp4,519.2bn is 1.14%; the data pack's Rp35.4bn is understated and is restated from the LK.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capital expenditure of Rp21.1bn [S2 p.152 note 39] on gross revenue of Rp4,519.2bn is 0.47%. A township developer's capex is infrastructure inside the estate, and the LK shows no step-up in the plan.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The ratio is set so working capital is a flat stock of rupiah, not a share of revenue, because the working capital is land-backed inventory and buyer advances and revenue is a handover schedule that swings 2.3x year to year. FY2026E carries the nine-month absorption observed in 2026: operating cash flow was about zero on nine-month EBITDA of Rp204.2bn while net debt rose from Rp241.2bn to Rp264.4bn (debt Rp765.0bn less cash Rp500.6bn) at 30 September 2026 [S0], and FY2025 net cash used in operating activities was Rp928.9bn [S2 p.45]. That absorption lifts operating working capital from Rp5,959.8bn to Rp6,204.1bn and lands FY2026E net debt at the reported Rp264.4bn with free cash flow of about zero, instead of the Rp244.3bn of cash a zero ratio would manufacture. FY2027E onward the stock is held flat in rupiah (the ratio falls as revenue grows), so delta_nwc is zero and the cash bridge carries no release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 income tax of Rp38.8bn on pre-tax profit of Rp254.6bn is 15.2% [S2 p.116]; property revenue also bears the final tax shown separately at Rp100.1bn, so the corporate rate stays low.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expenses of Rp40.8bn on opening bank debt of Rp400.0bn is about 10% [S2 p.144 note 20, p.35 note 35]; on FY2025 closing debt of Rp610.3bn, 7.8% is the effective rate the engine uses, consistent with the CIMB Niaga and BTN floating Rupiah facilities.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Financial income of Rp58.6bn on opening cash of Rp419.1bn is 14%, inflated by the significant-financing revenue line; the engine default of 3.7% is the cleaner run-rate and we keep it [S2 p.35 note 35, p.116].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt is Rp660.3bn at FY2025 and Rp765.0bn at 2026Q3 [S0, S2 p.144]; no refinancing need is disclosed and the 2025 rights issue funded a capital injection into the group's own subsidiaries [S2 p.51], so we model no net new borrowing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring non-operating line is disclosed. The FY2024 Rp1,701.2bn loss is the DINFRA/MSU common-control swap [S2 note 10.b, note 36]: MKCP took 99.92% of MSU by extinguishing the Bowsprit DINFRA investment at a fair value of Rp158.4bn and booked the difference, a related-party transaction we analyse in section 5 and price through the discount, not as a recurring item.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interest in the balance sheet is negative, at minus Rp38.1bn at 30 September 2026 [S0], and the minority share of profit was nil in the periods disclosed [S2 p.116], so minorities take nothing.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend was paid in FY2022-FY2025 and DPS TTM is zero [S0]; the stated policy pays 0-10% of net profit up to Rp800bn [S2 p.49], and the AGMS has retained everything. We model zero, consistent with the record, and treat any payout as upside.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares are 5,134.7m after the 2025 rights issue and no further corporate action is announced [S2 p.51]. The base case carries no issuance; the bear case carries the discounted rights issue the 9.33% float implies, and the bull case the tender that would close it.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2%, in line with the estate's occupied-area growth rather than nominal GDP, for a township developer whose revenue is shrinking back to its sales run-rate; the house default of 4% is too generous for this name.

challenges.challenge: RNAV adds the landbank gross of customer advances. Contract liabilities were Rp1,026.5bn current plus Rp846.6bn non-current at 30 Jun 2026 (Rp1,873.1bn, F15/F31); the method card defines RNAV as land bank less net debt AND advances, and CTRA, CBDK and MTLA all set landbank_value net of advances (CTRA's basis calls the gross treatment counting the same rupiah twice). Deducting Rp1,873.1bn takes RNAV from Rp8,318.2bn (Rp1,620/share) to Rp6,445.2bn (Rp1,255/share), the RNAV method from 729 to 565, v0 from 573 to 474 and the target from 520 to about 430 - +1.5% on Rp424, not +22.6%.
challenges.answer: Landbank now net of customer advances: inventories at 30 Sep 2026 plus land for development, less a 10% haircut, less total contract liabilities of Rp1,873.1bn (Rp1,026.5bn current plus Rp846.6bn non-current at 30 Jun 2026). Gross RNAV is Rp6,570.6bn, the RNAV method 575.8, v0 481.6 and the target 441. The FATAL is fixed, not argued.

challenges.challenge: Assets are taken at 31 Dec 2025 (inventories Rp8,404.5bn) while the liability side is 30 Sep 2026 (net debt Rp264.4bn = debt Rp765.0bn less cash Rp500.6bn) and advances 30 Jun 2026. Inventory had fallen to Rp7,713.8bn by Q3 2026, a Rp690.7bn decline the landbank ignores - the same date-mixing CTRA's basis identifies as an error. At the 10% haircut that is about Rp622bn of landbank, ~Rp121/share gross and ~Rp30/share of target.
challenges.answer: Every asset item now dates to 30 September 2026: inventories of Rp7,713.8bn from the pack's quarterly balance sheet replace the 31 Dec 2025 Rp8,404.5bn, on the same date as the net debt of Rp264.4bn. The decline is reflected in the landbank before the haircut, not ignored.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E EBITDA of Rp478.0bn is 2.3x the Rp204.3bn actually delivered in nine months (Q1 103.0, Q2 161.9, Q3 -60.6), so Q4 must produce Rp273.7bn - more than Q1+Q2 combined - after a Q3 EBIT of -Rp71.0bn and a net loss of Rp87.4bn. FY2026E revenue of Rp3,673.6bn against 9M of Rp2,375.3bn implies Q4 revenue of Rp1,298bn (+65% QoQ and +23% on FY2025Q4's Rp1,051.7bn) while Q3 was 33% below the prior-year quarter. The stated basis, that -19.5% 'is the nine-month run-rate annualised', is arithmetically false: annualising 9M total revenue gives Rp3,167bn, -28.3%.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is rebuilt from the nine months actually delivered plus a fourth quarter at the nine-month quarterly average, giving revenue and EBITDA far below the prior draft and a Q4 that no longer has to beat Q1+Q2 combined. The false basis text is deleted and replaced with the arithmetic.

challenges.challenge: FCFF is Rp844.7bn in FY2026E and Rp745.5bn in FY2027E on working-capital releases of Rp449.4bn and Rp438.9bn, produced by an nwc_pct held at the 1.5x-revenue default on a basis the analyst writes is 'meaningless here'. Actual 9M 2026 operating cash flow is about -Rp2.1bn (-55.7, -51.8, +105.4) and net debt rose from Rp241.2bn to Rp264.4bn, yet the model shows net cash of Rp572.8bn in FY2026E and Rp1,313.3bn in FY2027E.
challenges.answer: nwc_pct is set to zero so the cash bridge carries no working-capital release; FCFF, net debt and every DCF read are restated and the forecast no longer shows net cash in a year when nine-month operating cash flow was about zero and net debt rose. The basis now says the revenue ratio was the wrong driver.

challenges.challenge: The Rp1,701.2bn FY2024 DINFRA loss - 25% of FY2025 equity - is dismissed as 'a one-off settlement and is excluded'. The note shows a common-control business combination: MKCP acquired 99.92% of MSU by settling the DINFRA (Bowsprit Township Development) investment at a fair value of exchange of Rp158.4bn, booking a Rp1,701.2bn loss (S2 p.119, notes 36 and 43). The report names no counterparty, no assets received and no valuation, yet the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card calls related-party gravity the modal value-destruction channel on IDX.
challenges.answer: The FY2024 loss is analysed as a common-control business combination: MKCP took 99.92% of MSU by extinguishing the Bowsprit DINFRA investment at a disclosed exchange value, with the difference booked, no independent valuation and a related party that also sells commercial land to the company. Carried into the bear case as a structure flag.

challenges.challenge: The report says the 2025 rights issue 'funded the group's property injection' but never documents it: 100:111 at Rp500 is 2,701.2m new shares and Rp1,350.6bn of nominal capital, yet equity rose only Rp687.6bn in FY2025 (Rp5,999.0bn to Rp6,686.6bn) of which net profit is Rp215.8bn - leaving about Rp879bn of the stated issue size unexplained. Whether the shares were paid in cash, in kind from the controlling shareholder, or at what asset valuation decides whether the book behind the 20%-weighted P/BV method is land at cost or a related-party mark.
challenges.answer: The FY2025 statement of changes in equity is now shown: the limited public offering added share capital against a charge to additional paid-in capital for a net contribution of Rp473.4bn, which reconciles the share count. The proceeds went by capital injection into MKCP and on to MSU, with the working-capital portion two-thirds realised. No asset was taken in kind.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'RNAV per share is Rp729 before the developer discount. We apply 55.0%'. The engine's gross RNAV is Rp1,620.0/share and Rp729 is the value AFTER the 55% discount (valuation.methods.rnav.label: 'RNAV less target discount'). A reader following the stated build gets 729 x 0.45 x 0.8 = 262, not 520, and the same paragraph's claim that the two discounts put the effective discount 'at about 64%' contradicts its own arithmetic, which would be 84%.
challenges.answer: Section 4 is rewritten in the order the engine computes it: RNAV method after the discount, weighted value, roll-forward, liquidity discount to target. The claim that the stacked discount was about two-thirds is removed and the gross figure is no longer labelled as the post-discount one.

challenges.challenge: The bear case lands at Rp539 pre-liquidity, Rp431 after the 20% discount - 1.7% above the Rp424 price. A bear case that values the stock at what it costs is not a bear case, and because it is, the probability-weighted target (650) equals the base. The report also calls the float-driven corporate action 'likely and material' and says either route 'changes the per-share arithmetic', yet no scenario contains a discounted rights issue, a controller sell-down, an inventory write-down or a discount at the top of the 70% band.
challenges.answer: The bear case now lands below the price and carries the corporate action explicitly: presales lower, discount wider, landbank marked down and a share increase for a discounted rights issue. Probabilities unchanged; the weighted target is no longer equal to the base.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is only presales +8pp and the discount -10pp. Nothing is credited for the one event that would close the gap for this name: 89.0% control, a 9.33% float and a 2029 compliance deadline make a buyout, tender or controller-funded sell-down the obvious catalyst, and the controller itself subscribed at Rp500 in the 2025 rights issue - 18% above today's Rp424, evidence of the controller's own valuation that the report does not use.
challenges.answer: The bull case carries the float outcome as a share reduction, a tender by the controller, and the report uses the controller's own subscription price in the 2025 rights issue as its mark against today's price. The bear mirrors it with a share increase.

challenges.challenge: landbank_value is the 60%-weighted driver, and no scenario and no sensitivity moves it: bear and bull shock only presales_growth and rnav_discount, and the sensitivity grid is the same two. The report argues the 226 ha is serviced township land rather than raw kavling, then never quantifies it at a Cikarang land price, so neither the industrial/data-centre land upside in the bull narrative nor a land write-down is ever tested in the valuation.
challenges.answer: A landbank_value shock is added to both scenarios, mirrored, alongside presales and the discount, so a land write-down and a land mark-up are both tested. We found no sourced Cikarang land price per square metre in the archive, so the report says so plainly rather than inventing one; the sensitivity grid is industry-level config we cannot add an axis to.

challenges.challenge: The method card's output contract asks for interest coverage from recurring income only and the current discount against the name's own five-year band; neither is given. FY2025 recurring gross profit of Rp58.2bn against financial charges of Rp47.6bn is 1.2x before any recurring opex - the township-management stream does not cover interest - and the report substitutes group net debt/EBITDA of 0.9x, which is flattered by handover EBITDA. The 55% discount is called the band midpoint but is never set against the stock's own history.
challenges.answer: Interest cover from recurring income is shown two ways: about one and a fifth times on FY2025 support-services gross profit before its own costs, and several times over on the two half-year segment operating profits. The discount is set against the name's own five-year P/BV range and the RNAV band, with the current position stated.

challenges.challenge: The recurring stream is capitalised at 9% on GROSS profit: Rp64.0bn / 0.09 = Rp710.6bn added to RNAV, Rp138/share gross and 2.8x the Rp252.4bn carrying value of the investment properties that generate it. Gross profit is not net operating income - the segment's own costs sit in consolidated opex and are never deducted - so the claim that the 9% rate is 'deliberately conservative' is untested.
challenges.answer: The recurring stream is capitalised on segment operating profit, not gross: H1 2026 gross profit less the segment's own operating expenses, a conversion of about three-quarters, so the cap rate is a twelve per cent cap on that profit and about eight times segment earnings. The gross-equivalent rate the engine uses is stated in the params basis.

challenges.challenge: The method card says a KPI kill criterion on marketing sales is near-mandatory and its output contract wants the marketing-sales run-rate against target for the latest quarter. The report has neither: presales are flat at Rp1,301/1,643/1,649bn across three years against a Rp1,700bn 2026 target, the H1 2026 figure could not be sourced, and section 7 lists four numbers to watch without a trigger or a threshold.
challenges.answer: A dated kill criterion is added: a FY2026 marketing-sales print below the company target moves us to reduce regardless of asset value, tested at the full-year release and again at the results. The four monitored numbers now carry thresholds rather than being a list.

challenges.challenge: dev_gross_margin is set at 28.0% for FY2026E but justified against a BLENDED 29.9% H1 margin that includes the 12.3%-margin recurring segment; on the same split the H1 development margin is about 33%, so the input sits roughly 5pp below the last actual with no source, and the drift justification for the fade to 22% therefore compares a development-only number with a blended one.
challenges.answer: Development gross margin is set at the segment's own H1 2026 margin after final tax, taken from the segment note, not from the blended group figure, so the input sits at the last actual rather than five points below it. The drift justification is restated on the same development-only scope.

challenges.challenge: Two citation and format errors. F39 quotes S9 as 'wajib memenuhi ... 15 persen paling lambat pada 31 Maret 2027', but that date applies to issuers with a 12.5-15% float and at least Rp5tn of capitalisation; LPCK is the sub-Rp5tn tier whose date is 31 March 2029, which sections 5 and 6 state correctly, so the quote does not support the fact. And market capitalisation is written 'IDR2,177,106,733,408bn' in sections 4 and 5 when 5,134.7m shares at Rp424 is Rp2,177bn.
challenges.answer: F39 is requoted from the sub-Rp5tn transition sentence, which is the tier this issuer sits in, and the market capitalisation is written through the pack placeholder rather than as a malformed figure.

missing_bull_case.note: No value anywhere for a control/float event (89.0% held, 9.33% float, 31 Mar 2029 deadline) or for the controller's own Rp500 rights-issue subscription, 18% above the Rp424 price. Zero appraisal uplift on 226 ha, and landbank_value - the 60%-weighted driver - is shocked in no scenario and no sensitivity.

missing_bear_case.note: The Q3 2026 net loss of Rp87.4bn (EBIT -Rp71.0bn) is omitted; the Rp1,701.2bn DINFRA settlement loss is called a one-off with no counterparty analysis; recurring-only interest cover of 1.2x is absent; the float remedy the report calls 'likely' appears in no scenario.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E EBITDA of Rp478.0bn is 2.3x the Rp204.3bn delivered in nine months, requiring Q4 of Rp273.7bn; the Rp449bn FY2026E working-capital release comes from an nwc_pct the analyst calls 'meaningless here'; 9% is applied to gross profit, not NOI.

evidence_and_citations.note: F39 quotes the 12.5-15% / above-Rp5tn tier (2027) not LPCK's sub-Rp5tn tier (2029); the Rp1,350.6bn 2025 rights issue is never documented against a Rp687.6bn equity increase; the 9M revenue is cited while the 9M loss in the same pack is not.

valuation_method_fit.note: FATAL: RNAV adds the landbank gross of Rp1,873.1bn of contract liabilities although the method card and all three peer files (CTRA, CBDK, MTLA) deduct advances. Assets are dated 31 Dec 2025 and liabilities 30 Sep 2026, and Rp729 is described as pre-discount when it is post-discount.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims the base case follows the run-rate when it is 16% above it, and calls a bear case worth Rp431 against a Rp424 price a bear case. The 22.6% upside is the COE roll minus the liquidity discount, not an argued gap.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Peers deduct advances and LPCK does not; the report quotes a 5.8% policy rate and Rp17,570/USD while claiming the deck is used unchanged (deck 5.75% and 18,350); no marketing-sales run-rate against the Rp1,700bn target and no KPI kill criterion, both required by the card.

conservatism_audit.note: Two genuine haircuts: dev gross margin 28.0% versus a blended 29.9% H1 figure that implies about 33% on development alone (scope mismatch), and payout held at 0%. Both are small next to the optimism stack - revenue, opex and the gross-profit cap rate.

calibration.note: The ebitda_margin BLOCK is answered with H1 evidence that Q3 reverses, and the drift justification compares a development-only margin with a blended one. FY+1 does not reproduce the last actual or the 9M run-rate, so the gate is waved rather than met.

signoff.notes: Initiation HOLD, target Rp441 vs Rp424. Facts and lint PASS, no blocking gates. The judge too_bearish FAIL is answered on substance: the P/E method returns Rp214 because it applies the stock own 11.94x five-year mean to trailing earnings that carry the H2-2025 loss and a weak 2026 quarter, and section 4 discloses exactly that basis and brackets the answer from below rather than anchoring it; RNAV at 60% drives the blend. The earlier RNAV fault is fixed - the recurring stream is now capitalised at 15.7% on gross profit, a 12% cap on segment operating profit after its own cost load, against the prior 9% that valued it at nearly fifteen times net operating profit. The two remaining FIX items are addressed: opex_pct of 20.5% sits between the Q3-2026-inflated 22.9% nine-month and the clean 14.3% H1-2026 rate with the one-off disclosed, and the recurring-margin fade to 35% is justified against both half-year observations with the audited FY2025 12.3% explicitly rejected because it implies a second-half gross loss contradicting its own first half. NOTE, not blocking: the COE prose lists the 7.4% risk-free, 4.2% mature ERP, 2.5% CRP and 1.15 levered beta and says they give 13.5%, but as written they sum to 15.1% - the engine is right because it deducts the 1.6% sovereign default spread, as ROCK section 4 states, so add that clause. Number, target and rating do not move. Length 5,294 words.
